--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
GCC runtime libraries (Linux and macOS: bundled as unmodified shared libraries)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

libgfortran, libstdc++ and libgcc_s are part of GCC and are distributed under
the GNU General Public License, version 3, with the GCC Runtime Library
Exception, version 3.1, which permits their redistribution with programs
compiled by GCC under terms of the program's choosing. On Linux, libgfortran
is linked statically and libstdc++ is shipped as a shared library; on macOS,
libgfortran and libgcc_s are shipped as shared libraries.
https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gcc-exception-3.1.html

libquadmath is part of GCC and is distributed under the GNU Lesser General
Public License, version 2.1. On macOS it is shipped as the unmodified shared
library, which may be replaced by any compatible build. On Linux x86_64 the
parts libgfortran uses are linked statically; the complete source of these
programs and the scripts that build them are at
https://github.com/virtualcell/vcell-hy3s, so they can be relinked against a
modified libquadmath. libquadmath's source code is part of GCC:
https://gcc.gnu.org/

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Intel Fortran runtime (Windows executables, statically linked)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Windows executables are compiled with the Intel Fortran Compiler (ifx) and
contain portions of the Intel Fortran runtime libraries, redistributed under
the Intel End User License Agreement for Developer Tools, which permits their
redistribution as part of an application.
